answer: For each task, agents must lock a bond before their reports count; a randomly selected set of peers checks claims against evidence, and proven fabrication slashes the bond. Splitting one stake across many identities does not create more voting weight, so a Sybil attacker must commit more capital to sway results and risks losing it. On a ridge survey, for example, a false pulse reading can be checked against sensor records before an ember of reputation is earned.
